lab_questions.title: Detect Circular Microservice Dependencies
lab_questions.description:
A cloud microservices topology analyzer checks dependency relationships between N microservices (labeled 0 to N-1). A directed edge (u, v) indicates service u directly depends on service v. If a circular dependency exists (e.g., A -> B -> C -> A), the system will suffer a boot deadlock.

Read N (number of services) and M (number of dependency links), followed by M pairs of (u, v). Print CYCLE_DETECTED if a circular dependency is found, or SAFE if no cycles exist.

tasks.title: Test Case 1
tasks.description:
Validate your code against test case 1.
Input:
3 3
0 1
1 2
2 0
Expected Output: CYCLE_DETECTED

solution.python:
import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(2000)
data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
if data:
    n, m = data[0], data[1]
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    idx = 2
    for _ in range(m):
        u, v = data[idx], data[idx+1]
        adj[u].append(v)
        idx += 2
    visited = [0] * n
    has_cycle = False
    def dfs(u):
        nonlocal has_cycle
        visited[u] = 1
        for v in adj[u]:
            if visited[v] == 1:
                has_cycle = True
                return
            if visited[v] == 0:
                dfs(v)
        visited[u] = 2
    for i in range(n):
        if visited[i] == 0:
            dfs(i)
    print('CYCLE_DETECTED' if has_cycle else 'SAFE')
